title: Painters Gainesville FL vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Comparing Painters Gainesville FL and Precision Paint Experts for an older Gainesville home? What to ask about historic trim, wood siding, and period colors.
h1: Painters Gainesville FL vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Older Gainesville houses have wood siding, layered trim, and decades of paint history. This guide covers what to ask any painter before they work on one.

questions: How should old wood siding be prepared for paint?
What colors suit a historic Gainesville home?

body: Painters Gainesville FL is one of the painting companies that Gainesville homeowners may be comparing with Precision Paint Experts. We do not speak to other businesses' work. This page is aimed at owners of older houses, where the condition of the wood under the paint drives the whole project.

Clapboard and lap siding, deep window casings, porch columns, and decorative trim all add up to a lot of edges and a lot of places for moisture to get in. Old layers may be cracked or loose in spots and sound in others. The quality of the prep plan decides how the new finish will age.

Many owners of older homes are also keen to keep original materials where they can. Replacing a whole run of siding is rarely necessary when a few boards have failed, and a careful contractor will show you photos of the problem areas so you can decide together. That is how our crew leads approach the walkthrough: document first, then recommend.

sections.h2: Questions specific to historic and older homes
body: Put these to each contractor and look for the answers in the written scope:
bullets: How will loose and failing paint be removed: scraping, sanding, or both?
Will rotted clapboards, sills, or fascia be replaced, and how is that approved?
Which primer goes on bare wood exposed during prep?
Is the work sprayed, brushed, or both, and is spray back-brushed into the laps?
What color guidance is offered for the home's style?

sections.h2: Our prep and coating plan for older wood
body: A crew lead from Precision Paint Experts photographs conditions and takes moisture readings where boards look suspect. Prep days cover washing, mildew treatment, scraping, sanding, nail pops, rot and fascia replacement, re-caulking, and spot-priming, all spelled out on the estimate.

Siding and trim get 100% acrylic from premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines, with two full coats as the baseline and a third on porous substrates. Where we spray, we back-brush or back-roll so paint gets into the laps and grain. Our article on hidden moisture damage behind siding explains what we are looking for during the walkthrough.

Older homes often look best in palettes that suit their era rather than whatever is trending. Our piece on historic paint colors for Gainesville homes is a useful starting point, and our color consultation in Gainesville can narrow the choice with full-size drawdowns on your siding and trim. We can also match an existing color from a chip or a piece of trim.
Porches deserve their own plan. Ceilings, floors, columns, and railings each need a different product, and the estimate should list them separately so nothing is skipped.

sections.h2: Schedule a walkthrough of your older home
body: October through May is the best window for exterior work in Gainesville. A full exterior usually takes three to seven working days plus washing and dry time, and it is backed by a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years. faqs.q: Do you replace rotted siding boards before painting?
faqs.a: Yes, rot and fascia replacement is part of our prep where needed. Each repair is listed on the estimate, and nothing is added later without your written approval.

faqs.q: Do you spray or brush older wood siding?
faqs.a: It depends on the surface. Where we spray, we back-brush or back-roll so the coating penetrates the laps and grain.

faqs.q: Can you match a color from my existing trim?
faqs.a: Yes. We match from a chip, a painted piece, or a leftover can and confirm with full-size drawdowns.
